newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - March 26.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - March 26.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Wednesday:

* Indonesia's central bank is confident this year's general election and next year's presidential election will not put much pressure on the country's balance of payments, central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said on Tuesday, adding the international community shared its confidence.

* The Finance Ministry has issued a new regulation prohibiting new link-ups between two or more cigarette firms be it in the form of capital, production, marketing or management, Bisnis Indonesia newspaper reported. It said cigarette firms with such arrangements have two years to adhere to the ruling.

* On Tuesday, the Dow Jones industrial average closed down 29.08 points at 6,876.17 as Wall Street briefly cheered an interest rate increase by the Federal Reserve but then quickly worried that further hikes could depress economic growth.

* In a widely anticipated move, the Fed raised the key federal funds rate by a quarter percentage point to 5.50 percent -- the first increase since Feb. 1, 1995 -- in an effort to stay a step ahead of inflation. The federal funds rate is the rate banks charge each other for overnight loans.
* On Tuesday, the Jakarta Composite Index closed 7.67 points higher at 657.29 points
* On Wednesday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,397.50/98.00 at 0140 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,398.00/98.25
* Modernland on market talk of a possible link-up with a Japanese property firm.
* Duta Pertiwi after its shareholders on Tuesday approved the firm's proposed rights issue.

* Cigarette firms Sampoerna and Gudang Garam on reports of a new government regulation prohibiting link-ups between two or more cigarette firms be it in the form of capital, production, marketing or management.
